answer: We move growing US businesses from Zoho CRM to Dynamics 365 Sales: your leads, contacts, accounts, deals and history, with record counts checked against Zoho before go-live. Moving data from your old CRM or spreadsheets is part of a full implementation. Microsoft licenses are a separate cost, and support plans start at $500 a month.

price_h: What do Dynamics 365 Sales and Zoho CRM cost per user?
price_lead: Microsoft lists Dynamics 365 Sales at $65, $105 or $150 per user per month, paid yearly. Zoho lists Zoho CRM Standard at $14, Professional at $23 and Enterprise at $40 per user per month billed annually, or $20, $35 and $50 billed monthly, and a free edition for up to 3 users.

price_note2: Zoho also has an Ultimate edition for large deployments; its US pricing page does not show a price for it. Zoho says local taxes may apply.
fit_lead: A move fits a sales team on Zoho CRM whose setup is mostly standard records, such as leads, contacts, accounts and deals, and who already work in Outlook and Teams. It is a weaker fit if your Zoho CRM account runs many blueprints, custom functions and connected apps, or if you need other systems connected on day one.
fit_yes: Most of your Zoho CRM setup is standard records: leads, contacts, accounts and deals.
Your Zoho renewal date is coming and you want a plan before it arrives.
fit_no: Your Zoho CRM account runs many blueprints, custom functions and connected apps. We review them first and scope that rebuild separately.
q4: Do our Zoho workflows and blueprints move across?
Not on their own. Workflows, blueprints, custom functions and connected apps are rebuilt in Dynamics 365 rather than copied. We review them first and quote any rebuild separately.
q5: Does Microsoft have a tool for moving from Zoho CRM?

Not a dedicated one. Microsoft's own migration tool, Dynamics 365 Activate, covers moves from Salesforce. For other systems, Microsoft's guidance points to data import, dataflows and data migration tools such as Azure Data Factory.

live_page_notes: Read 9 Nov 2026 via WebFetch (curl to encloud9.com is blocked by the proxy here). Title: 'Easily Migrate from Zoho CRM to Dynamics 365 with enCloud9'. H1: 'Outgrowing Zoho CRM? Find a CRM That Matches Your Vision'. Sections: checklist offer ('Ensure a Smooth CRM Transition. Get the Zoho CRM to Dynamics 365 Checklist.'), a 'Zoho CRM vs. Dynamics 365' table, 'Leave Zoho CRM Behind' with two blocks (Built around your business, Insights that drive action), a four-step process (Data Mapping & Cleansing, Migration Execution, Configuration & Customization, Training & Adoption Support), 'It's Simple – Dynamics 365 is Better.' with five benefits (reporting, workflows, Microsoft integration, AI, scalability), and a closing 'Let's Chat' CTA. Download form: first name, last name, work email, consent; button 'Get My Free Download!'. CTA button 'Book Your Strategy Call!' with a phone emoji, linking to an Outlook booking page (not the /lp/schedule-a-meeting/ page). Header phone 1-844-264-0729. Errors and unsourced claims: (1) the comparison table rates Zoho CRM limited or partial on ten rows (customization, Microsoft 365 integration, pricing flexibility, data ownership, Power BI, AI tools, multi-entity support, workflow automation, enterprise features, migration help) with no source; Zoho's own page lists workflow automation in every edition, Outlook and Teams integration in Standard, AI agents in Professional, and custom functions in Enterprise, so several ratings conflict with the vendor's page; (2) 'Dynamics 365 is Better' and 'Leave Zoho CRM Behind' break the house rule on 'better than' claims; (3) em and en dashes in two headings; (4) uses the old name 'Office 365'; (5) no prices, no package scope, no timeline; (6) booking CTA points at an Outlook page, not the standard booking URL.
notes: Zoho prices are geo-based: a server-side fetch returned INR from an India view; the US figures were read in the browser on zoho.com/en-us with the Annually and Monthly toggles each confirmed on screen. Zoho also shows Bigin Express (US$7 annual, US$9 monthly) and Zoho One (from $30); both are separate products and are left out of the rows. Ultimate edition has no US price on the page, noted in price_note2. Zoho states no onboarding fee (it advertises Free Onboarding), so col5 is 'AI on the vendor's page' as on the Salesforce page, and the Microsoft rows copy the Salesforce sister page exactly.
